title: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)

sections.label: Future-ready education and CET system
sections.summary: The speaker moves to reduce Head K by $100, citing an urgent need for a future-ready education and CET system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head K of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Sir, with the half-life of skills shortening in an increasingly disruptive, transformative, highly unpredictable and uncertain world and future upon us, I see an urgent imperative for Singapore to build and forge an even more future-ready and future-proof education system – one that encourages a learning continuum where our education system and a Continuing Education and Training (CET) ecosystem where our teachers and adult educators, our students and our adult learners are seamlessly aligned and well-connected to be best prepared for the future of skills, jobs, education and training.

sections.label: The next normal
sections.summary: The next normal is described as alternating cycles of learning and working, then perhaps retiring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The next normal will be "learn, work, learn, work, learn, work and then, perhaps, retire".

sections.label: Learning beyond age limits
sections.summary: Technology-enhanced learning will flow to informal contexts and shift from upfront qualification-oriented attainment to a new distribution of learning and skill development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Enhanced by technology, learning will gradually flow to informal contexts and move beyond age defined limitations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: We will shift from qualification oriented attainment upfront to a new distribution of learning and skill development.

sections.label: Teachers' mental well-being study
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOE to study teachers' and educators' stress, mental health and wellness with tripartite partners to provide better interventions and support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am particularly concerned with the mental well-being of our teachers, as well as adult educators, in light of such curveballs constantly hurled at them and having had to cope with the demands and expectations of students, learners, the administration as well as parents, and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I therefore urge MOE to embark on an in-depth study and survey of our teachers and educators, together with our tripartite partners to better assess the current state of stress, mental health, and wellness of our education fraternity so that better interventions and support can be provided for them in their teaching journey.

sections.label: Educators using right technology
sections.summary: Educators need to not just use technology but make use of the right technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Educators also need to not just use technology but make use of the right technology.

sections.label: NTUC CET study findings
sections.summary: NTUC's study of 564 business leaders found five key findings on CET, and MOE and SkillsFuture can leverage NTUC's ecosystem with $100 million from Budget 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: On the adult learner front, NTUC recently embarked on a study with 564 business leaders across industries, looking into how CET can be enhanced to upskill our workers to meet the needs of today's and tomorrow's labour market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The five key findings revealed: (a) skills mismatch continues to be the most prevalent form of mismatch; (b) the top five transferable skills sought after by business leaders are adaptability, customer orientation, communication, problem solving and collaboration; (c) only 50.9% of business leaders have sent their workers for training in the past six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Out of those business leaders who sent workers for training, only 33.6% of their workforce actually attended training; (d) workers with skills gaps are not the top priority for training as compared to workers with higher potential; and (e) majority of the business leaders are reported to have observe positive changes in their workers post training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: With the $100 million announced at Budget 2022 to support the Labour Movement in our company training committee formation and CET, MOE and SkillsFuture can now leverage on NTUC's training and placement ecosystem as a strategic partner to drive the CET agenda for workers and adult learners.

sections.label: Frontloading of education must change
sections.summary: The frontloading of education, which crams most learning before one's first job, has to change.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The frontloading of education – cramping most of learning before one’s first job – has to change.

sections.label: Lifelong Learning Participation Rate KPI
sections.summary: The Minister spoke about replacing cohort thinking and Cohort Participation Rates with a Lifelong Learning Participation Rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Minister spoke about having to stop thinking of educating cohorts and the traditional KPI of "Cohort Participation Rates" and replace it with the concept of "Lifelong Learning Participation Rate".

sections.label: Pilot through-train schools without PSLE
sections.summary: The writer suggests piloting through-train schools without the PSLE and letting go of the PSLE if it is a sacred cow.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For instance, pilot through-train schools without the PSLE – an idea I brought up for years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If PSLE, regardless of what the MOE has tried, is still a sacred cow and if slain, can free time and space for change, then let go of it!

sections.label: OECD adviser on older workers
sections.summary: Andreas Schleicher observed a skills gap between younger and older Singapore workers and advised developing older workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Andreas Schleicher, OECD’s Special Adviser, has observed the striking skills gap between Singapore’s younger and older workforce, and he advised the strong need for Singapore to seriously develop our older workers.

sections.label: MOE removed Primary 1 and 2 exams
sections.summary: MOE removed exams for Primary 1 and Primary 2 to let children grow without major exam pressures and burdens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Some time ago, MOE took the step of removing exams for Primary 1 and Primary 2 to allow for a learning experience and learning environment that would allow children to grow and develop without having to deal with the pressures and burdens of major exams.

sections.label: Review of summative assessments
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government would review having less summative and more formative assessments across Primary and up to Secondary levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Government review the need to have less summative assessments across all levels of Primary school even up to Secondary school levels, and move towards having more formative assessments that cater to more holistic and complete development of our students?

sections.label: Reducing school curriculum content
sections.summary: A speaker urges schools and tertiary institutions to reduce subject content, noting past curriculum cuts did not lessen student stress or workload.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: MOE had previously said that they had reduced 20% of the school curriculum under the “Teach Less Learn More” initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: However, the previous reduction in curriculum had not resulted in less stress or less workload for the students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Hence, I urge the schools and tertiary institutions to consider reducing the content of the subjects taught to the students.

sections.label: Teaching emotional wellness and resilience
sections.summary: The passage asks how emotional wellness and resilience can be taught, including handling failure, disappointment and not being liked.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How may we truly teach emotional wellness and resilience: that it is okay to not be liked all the time, that it is okay not to be perfect.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How does one teach children to think for themselves, shrug off failure, handle disappointment, and to have the strength and courage to keep on going.

sections.label: Tharman on evolving Singapore parenting
sections.summary: In previous speeches, Mr Tharman spoke on how Singapore parents must evolve and avoid helicopter parenting.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In previous speeches, Mr Tharman spoke on how Singapore parents must evolve, and avoid the trend of helicopter parenting.

sections.label: Letting children make own decisions
sections.summary: A speaker says children must be taught independence, make their own decisions, accept consequences, and parents should stop pursuing a perfect checklist.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I need to teach them to be independent.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I know it is hard, but we have to let our children make their own decisions and accept the consequences of their actions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Fellow parents, let us stop pursuing the perfect checklist, and truly enable our children to be ready to face the challenges of the real world.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Those in favour have cited evidence, which was compelling in my view, that phase delays in adolescent Circadian rhythms predisposed them towards sleeping and waking later, typically by about two hours, although some, like my sister, appear to have never grown up and exited this phase.

sections.label: Later start times and sleep
sections.summary: Students with later start times sleep longer, with bedtimes unchanged or delayed less than the extra time gained.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Students who have later start times sleep longer, with bedtimes that either remain unchanged or delayed by a smaller amount than the additional time afforded.

sections.label: Teenagers from high-ranked schools
sections.summary: One study placed the proportion at 80% of Singaporean teenagers from high-ranked schools.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One study placed this proportion at a staggering 80% of Singaporean teenagers hailing from high-ranked schools.

sections.label: Later school start times
sections.summary: Proposes delaying upper Primary start times by half an hour and Secondary start times by an hour, making 8.00 am and 8.30 am.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Delay upper Primary school start time by half an hour and Secondary school start time by an hour.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For schools currently starting at 7.30 am, the earliest start time at the moment, this would mean a meantime of 8.00 am for the Primary cohort and 8.30 am for the Secondary cohort.

sections.label: 10-year through-train programme
sections.summary: Urges MOE to consider a pilot 10-year through-train programme for Primary and Secondary students, bypassing the PSLE.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Today, I wish to again urge MOE to consider implementing a pilot project of a 10-year through-train programme for Primary and Secondary school students, bypassing the PSLE.

sections.label: Madrasah barred from Primary 1
sections.summary: A madrasah missed MOE's benchmark in 2008 and 2010, so it was barred from taking Primary 1 students from 2012 to 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Regrettably, a madrasah was not able to meet MOE’s benchmark in 2008 and 2010, which resulted in the madrasah being barred from taking in Primary 1 students from 2012 to 2014.

sections.label: Reviewing MOE madrasah benchmark
sections.summary: Asks MOE to work with MUIS and madrasahs to review the benchmark, considering removal, easing, or warnings with independent audits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Although the MOE benchmark was born out of good intentions, it may cause undue stress for the madrasah administrators and teachers, as well as for madrasah students and their parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is because the MOE benchmark disallows a madrasah to take in Primary 1 pupils for three years if it fails to meet the benchmark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As such, I would like to ask MOE to work with MUIS and the madrasahs to review the necessity of this benchmark and to consider either removing it completely or easing the benchmark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Alternatively, instead of the two mentioned options, the Ministry could also consider issuing warnings to the madrasahs that do not meet the benchmark, accompanied by a requirement for them to conduct an independent audit of its practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Chairman, full Subject Based Banding (SBB) was implemented in 28 Secondary schools from 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Students are grouped in different classes for both STEM and Humanities subjects, according to the levels at which students take them.

sections.label: Removal of secondary school courses
sections.summary: MOE has committed that from 2024 the Express, Normal (Academic) and Normal (Technical) courses will be removed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: The MOE has committed that from 2024, the Express, Normal (Academic) and Normal (Technical) courses will be removed.

sections.label: English use at home
sections.summary: Based on the 2020 Population Census, 48.3% of residents used English most frequently at home in 2020, compared to 32.3% in 2010.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Chairman, based on the 2020 Population Census, more residents are using English as the most frequently used language at home, that is 48.3% in 2020 as compared to 32.3% in 2010.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credits for younger Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister will consider extending SkillsFuture credits to younger Singaporeans, perhaps from age 18 or 21.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Will the Minister consider extending SkillsFuture credits to younger Singaporeans perhaps from the age of 18 or 21?

sections.label: CCA instructors and new contract mode
sections.summary: The passage states that pay-per-use contracting caused many CCA instructors to leave, and notes a new contract mode ensuring minimum contracted CCA hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As a result of the pay-per-use contracting model, many CCA instructors had to leave the industries as it is no longer viable with the number of paid CCA hours greatly reduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is indeed heartening that there is an implementation of a new contract mode that ensures a minimum level of commitment towards contracted CCA hours.

sections.label: Term based on key milestones
sections.summary: The passage proposes a term based on key milestones and development runway for NSG and SYF instead of a short-term period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Instead of a short-term period, which increases the chances of disruptions to students’ learning experience, I propose a term that is based on key milestones and development runway for events such as National School Games (NSG) and Singapore Youth Festival (SYF).

sections.label: Recognising instructors through intellectual property
sections.summary: The passage seeks MOE recognition of instructors' value of work through intellectual property and copyrights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Thirdly, I seek MOE to recognise instructors’ value of work through intellectual property and copyrights.

sections.label: Industry attachments for teachers
sections.summary: The passage says many teachers may lack exposure to other industries and suggests MOE explore industry attachments for their development and classroom contextualisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: As such, many of them might not have had much opportunity or exposure to other industries or professional environments before they become teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: It would thus be good if MOE could explore industry attachments, not only for the teachers’ own personal and professional development, but also so that they can contextualize the subjects that they are teaching in the classrooms to the students.

sections.label: Supporting teachers' well-being
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry is supporting and managing teachers' well-being, saying the experience will rejuvenate them and inject fresh ideas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: This experience will rejuvenate them and help them to inject fresh ideas into their work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Thus, I would like to ask, how is the Ministry supporting and managing teachers' well-being?

sections.label: Teacher grading quota removal
sections.summary: Speaker hopes MOE will remove grade quotas, set objective criteria for grades A, C and E, drop punitive implications and allow development leave for C- grades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: After one year of further engagement, I hope MOE will remove the quota for grades, provide objective criteria for certain performance grades, starting with A, C and E; remove punitive implications of getting lower grades and allow for professional development leaves for those who get C- grades.

sections.label: Teacher working hours and counselling
sections.summary: A 2019 study found Singapore teachers' working hours exceed the OECD average, and teachers seeking MOE counselling have almost doubled since before COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A 2019 study already found that working hours of Singapore teachers is higher than the OECD average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The average number of teachers seeking support through MOE's counselling services has almost doubled from before COVID-19.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements for teachers
sections.summary: Speaker asks whether MOE can require all schools to offer flexible work arrangements, including staggered hours and allowing teachers to leave when no school matters remain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can MOE require all schools to offer FWAs, including staggered working hours and allow teachers to leave as long as there are no matters to take care of in school?

sections.label: School admissions socio-economic data
sections.summary: Speaker filed a Parliamentary Question seeking data on socio-economic backgrounds of students admitted to Government, Government-aided and Independent secondary schools, but the data was not released.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I filed a Parliamentary Question last November, asking for data on the socio-economic backgrounds of students admitted into different categories of Secondary schools, such as Government, Government-aided and Independent categories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the Government gave a response describing the school admissions process, it did not release the data I asked for.

sections.label: ITE and Polytechnic apprenticeships
sections.summary: Speaker asks whether the Ministry can consider longer apprenticeship schemes for ITE and Polytechnic students to work with industry staff and gain job-specific skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For students in our ITE or Polytechnics, can the Ministry consider apprenticeship schemes where students can work with experienced staff from industry partners for a longer duration, as compared to internships so that they can learn job specific skills and gain applied competency?

sections.label: 2021 graduate employment survey results
sections.summary: The 2021 graduate employment survey found more university graduates in full-time employment with higher salaries, and Polytechnic improvements, but ITE results were not released.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the latest graduate employment survey for 2021, it was found that more university graduates secured full-time employment, with salaries also increasing as Singapore’s economy recovered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Polytechnics have also shown improvements in employment rates and salaries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, the results for ITE have not been released.

sections.label: SkillsFuture spending per adult
sections.summary: MOE estimates about $1.3 billion for SkillsFuture programmes in FY2022, averaging $542 per resident working adult, compared with $16,000 per child and $22,000 per university student.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Based on MOE’s estimated expenditure for Financial Year 2022, about $1.3 billion will be spent on SkillsFuture-related programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: This represents about less than 10% of the total MOE Expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Yet this amount is supposed to support 2.4 million resident working adults, averaging $542 per worker.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: This contrasts starkly with the amount of about $16,000 per child up to Secondary level and about $22,000 per full-time University student.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: What would be a more reasonable amount of CET spend per adult to achieve the outcomes we intend?

sections.label: Measuring certification value and stackability
sections.summary: The passage asks how MOE measures the value of certification or programmes after completion and ensures courses are compatible or stackable toward academic or professional certification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: How is MOE measuring the value of the certification or programme post its completion?

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: How does MOE ensure compatibility or stackability of courses toward an academic or professional certification?

sections.label: SPED graduates' prognosis
sections.summary: The passage states that SPED graduates' prognosis is not as positive as expected despite more MOE funding, controls, pay and seconded mainstream principals and teachers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: The prognosis of SPED graduates is not as positive as expected in spite of more MOE funding, more MOE controls, more pay and more seconded MOE mainstream principals and teachers.

sections.label: Special Education Academy proposal
sections.summary: With 80% of students with special education needs in mainstream schools, the passage proposes setting up a Special Education Academy to uplift them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: With 80% of students with special education needs in Singapore's mainstream schools, SPED schools can become the precious resource to uplift them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Set up a Special Education Academy for that.

sections.label: EIPIC wait times and capacity
sections.summary: The passage notes EIPIC wait times of three to 18 months and limited weekly hours, and asks if ECDA can work with providers to increase capacity and services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While ECDA does provide subsidised support through the Early Intervention Programme for Infants & Children (EIPIC) programme, EIPIC centres have wait times ranging from three to 18 months and most provide a limited number of hours of intervention a week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This requires parents to turn to additional services that can cost thousands more every month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can ECDA work with EIPIC providers to increase the capacity and range of services provided so that children can receive all the early intervention support they require from the same centre?

sections.label: TRANSIT implementation update
sections.summary: The passage asks for an update on implementation of MOE's Transition Support for Integration (TRANSIT) and whether there are plans to expand it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: MOE had previously announced Transition Support for Integration or TRANSIT to help children ease the transition into Primary school.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Could I get an update on the implementation of TRANSIT and find out if there are any plans on the expansion of this programme?

sections.label: COVID-19 school staff workload
sections.summary: Over two years of COVID-19 disruptions, staff took on extra workload and went beyond duty to keep children safe and schools open.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In the past two years of COVID-19 disruptions, they have taken on additional workload and have gone beyond the call of duty to keep our children safe, our schools open and our learning undisrupted.

sections.label: Education system vision elements
sections.summary: The education system vision has three elements: develop confident Singaporeans, build a competitive Singapore, and forge a cohesive society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Chair, our vision of our education system has three elements: to develop confident Singaporeans; to build a competitive Singapore; and to forge a cohesive society.

sections.label: Connectivity dimensions
sections.summary: Connectivity refers to physical air, land and sea dimensions, non-physical data, finance, rules and technology, and ideas, cultures and values.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: By connectivity, I refer not just to the physical dimensions of air, land and sea, not even the non-physical dimensions of data, finance, rules and technology; but also of ideas, cultures and values.

sections.label: Life course approach to education
sections.summary: A life course approach to education will be taken, so that MOE for schools becomes MOE for life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: It is the substrate upon which our new ideas grow.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Therefore, Chair, we will take a life course approach to education. “MOE for schools" must become “MOE for life”.

sections.label: Preschool investment and framework
sections.summary: Investments in quality affordable preschools are being made, and the Nurturing Early Learners Framework is being updated to emphasise social and emotional skills and core values.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We have invested in many quality and affordable preschools, where our children can enjoy and learn through play, develop early literacy and numeracy, as well as social and emotional skills, ask questions and explore their interests, and most importantly – ignite their innate curiosity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We are updating the Nurturing Early Learners Framework to guide our preschool educators, to incorporate social and emotional skills even more prominently and emphasise core values of respect, responsibility, care, and honesty from young.

sections.label: Removing mid-year examinations
sections.summary: Mid-year examinations for all Primary and Secondary levels will be removed by 2023, building on gains so students focus more on learning than marks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Students also focus more on their learning and less on marks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will build on these gains, by removing mid-year examinations for all Primary and Secondary levels by 2023.

sections.label: Home-Based Learning for students
sections.summary: Regular Home-Based Learning will be implemented for all Secondary and pre-university students by end-2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Regular Home-Based Learning will be implemented for all Secondary and pre-university students by end-2022.

sections.label: Expanding Full Subject-Based Banding
sections.summary: Full Subject-Based Banding will be expanded for more porous and diverse educational pathways, encouraging students to take greater ownership of their education journey.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In line with these principles, we will expand Full Subject-Based Banding (Full SBB) for more porous and diverse educational pathways and encourage students to take greater ownership of their education journey.

sections.label: Discontinuing MTL B
sections.summary: With Full SBB, students can study MTL at G1 or G2 level, so MTL "B" will be discontinued from the 2024 Secondary 1 cohort.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: With Full SBB, they can now study MTL at a level that better meets their learning needs – whether G1 or G2.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will thus discontinue MTL "B" from the 2024 Secondary 1 cohort.

sections.label: Express-only schools named
sections.summary: Crescent Girls' School, Tanjong Katong Girls' School and Tanjong Katong Secondary School currently admit only students in the Express stream.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Crescent Girls’ School, Tanjong Katong Girls’ School and Tanjong Katong Secondary School currently admit only students in the Express stream.

sections.label: Expanding Polytechnic Foundation Programme
sections.summary: The Polytechnic Foundation Programme will be expanded and selected grade requirements relaxed from Academic Year 2024, with another 200 students expected to benefit yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: First, we will expand the Polytechnic Foundation Programme (PFP) and relax selected grade requirements for entry from Academic Year 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: A wider group of learner profiles can benefit from a practice-based preparatory pathway to the polytechnics, while still ensuring that students can cope with the rigour.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We expect another 200 students every year to benefit, in addition to the 1,500 today.

sections.label: DSA intake for JCs
sections.summary: Starting from 2022, these JCs can admit up to 20% of their non-Integrated Programme intake through DSA, up from 10% today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Starting from 2022, these JCs can admit up to 20% of their non-Integrated Programme intake through DSA, up from 10% today.

sections.label: overseas experience 70 by 70 target
sections.summary: IHLs will work towards the 70 by 70 target disrupted by COVID-19, with 70% of students having an overseas experience, 70% in ASEAN, China and India.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In this same spirit, our IHLs will continue to work towards the 70 by 70 target disrupted by COVID-19 – 70% of all students will have an overseas experience, of which 70% will be in ASEAN countries, China and India.

sections.label: EMAS expansion to Raffles Institution
sections.summary: EMAS is offered at three host schools today and will expand to a fourth host centre, Raffles Institution, from 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: EMAS is offered at three host schools today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will expand EMAS to a fourth host centre, Raffles Institution, from 2023 so that more students can access it, including students from other nearby schools.

sections.label: skills training spending increase
sections.summary: In 2021, nearly $1.2 billion was spent on skills training for the workforce, 40% more than 2019, excluding COVID-19-related programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In 2021, we spent nearly $1.2 billion in skills training for our workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This is 40% more than 2019 and it excludes spending on COVID-19-related programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will do more to support Singaporeans to achieve greater career resilience and job mobility through a major investment in skills refresh.

sections.label: SGUS and SGUP-CT transition
sections.summary: SGUnited Skills and SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways – Company Training programmes will close and transit to a new SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: During the pandemic, to help mid-career individuals move to new sectors or job roles, we introduced the SGUnited Skills (SGUS) and SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways – Company Training (SGUP-CT) programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will bring these programmes to a close and transit to a new SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme (SCTP).

sections.label: adult learners trained increase
sections.summary: Adult learners trained by institutions more than doubled from around 165,000 in 2018 to 345,000 in 2020, and the number is expected to rise further.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: While the number of adult learners trained by our institutions has more than doubled from around 165,000 in 2018 to 345,000 in 2020, we can expect this number to go up further.

sections.label: work-study programmes mainstream pathway
sections.summary: By 2025, work-study programmes will cater to 12% of each cohort, up from 4% today, with support for industry partners and micro-credentials.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: By 2025, work-study programmes will be a mainstream pathway catering to 12% of each cohort, up from 4% today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will support industry partners to develop in-house on-the-job training capabilities through the National Centre of Excellence for Workplace Learning.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Industry can also offer industry micro-credentials that are recognised by employers alongside our institutions' credentials.

sections.label: TechSkills and Manufacturing Grants
sections.summary: Some initiatives were announced at recent MCI and MTI Committees of Supply, including TeSA and the Accelerated Pathways Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Some of these initiatives were announced at the recent MCI's and MTI's Committees of Supply, such as the TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) for ITE and Polytechnics Aliiance, and the Accelerated Pathways for Technicians & Assistant Engineers (Manufacturing) Grant.

sections.label: Teacher Work Attachment Plus
sections.summary: Through the Teacher Work Attachment Plus programme, teachers can broaden perspectives, enhance skills and build connections.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Through the Teacher Work Attachment Plus programme, our teachers can broaden their perspectives, enhance their skills and build connections.

sections.label: Educator Appraisal Consistency and Fairness
sections.summary: The appraisal system must ensure consistency and fairness in the ranking of educators.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Our appraisal system must, therefore, ensure consistency and fairness in the ranking of our educators.

sections.label: Partners, Instructors and Success Definition
sections.summary: MOE and partners recognise instructors' role, review procurement and contracts for COVID-19, and success must evolve beyond grades.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: MOE and our partners, like SportSG, the National Arts Council and the National Instructors & Coaches Association, recognise the important role they play.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We have platforms for regular engagements and have been working closely with them, including reviewing our procurement processes and contractual terms to mitigate the impact of COVID-19, and we will continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As Dr Tan Yia Swam said earlier, all of us want the best for our children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But our definition of success must evolve beyond just getting good grades in examinations.

sections.label: Community Partnership for Higher-Needs Students
sections.summary: In the spirit of it taking a village to raise a child, the community is partnered to support students with higher needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As they say, “it takes a village to raise a child.” In this spirit, we partner the community to support our students with higher needs, including through UPLIFT, ComLink and other efforts.

sections.label: UPLIFT Taskforce Initiative
sections.summary: A key initiative undertaken is UPLIFT, the Uplifting Pupils in Life and Inspiring Families Taskforce.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: A key initiative we have undertaken is UPLIFT, or Uplifting Pupils in Life and Inspiring Families Taskforce.

sections.label: UPLIFT Enhanced School Resourcing expansion
sections.summary: UPLIFT Enhanced School Resourcing gives schools extra manpower, guidance and teaching resources, supporting 47 schools now, expanding to 100 schools for around 13,000 students.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We will support our schools in doing so.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We introduced UPLIFT Enhanced School Resourcing to provide schools with additional manpower, guidance and teaching resources to help students with higher needs more effectively.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Forty-seven schools are currently supported under this initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We plan to expand this to 100 schools in total over the next few years to support around 13,000 students.

sections.label: UPLIFT Community Network nationwide support
sections.summary: When rolled out nationwide, the UPLIFT Community Network will support 1,800 students and their families each year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Eventually, when it is rolled out nationwide, 1,800 students and their families will be supported by the UPLIFT Community Network each year.

sections.label: Support for students with greater needs
sections.summary: Initiatives highlighted will strengthen support to students with greater needs, especially those from challenging backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, through the various initiatives I have highlighted, we will strengthen support to students with greater needs, especially those from challenging backgrounds.

sections.label: Refreshed Character and Citizenship Education curriculum
sections.summary: Managing emotions, seeking help and navigating online space safely are taught under the refreshed Character and Citizenship Education curriculum.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: They also need to be able to manage their emotions, seek help when needed and navigate online space safely.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: These topics are taught under the refreshed Character and Citizenship Education, or CCE, curriculum.

sections.label: Teacher mental health literacy and counselling
sections.summary: Teachers' mental health literacy will be developed and counselling resources increased, with 700 teacher counsellors now and 360 more planned.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We will continue to develop our teachers’ mental health literacy, so they understand and recognise symptoms related to common mental health issues early.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We are also increasing counselling resources to our schools.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Beyond school counsellors deployed in every school, we are equipping teachers to help students with more challenging mental health issues and adjusting their teaching workload accordingly.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We currently have 700 teacher counsellors and plan to deploy an additional 360 over the next few years.

sections.label: Personal tutors for Polytechnic and ITE students
sections.summary: Each Polytechnic and ITE student is assigned a personal tutor for guidance and support.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Each Polytechnic and ITE student is assigned a personal tutor, who they can turn to for guidance and support.

sections.label: Polytechnic admissions and modular loads
sections.summary: 20% of each Polytechnic intake enters through aptitude-based admissions, and from AY2022 Polytechnics will pilot flexible modular loads for students needing time for foundations or side interests.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Today, 20% of each Polytechnic intake enters through the aptitude-based admissions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: From Academic Year (AY) 2022, all Polytechnics will pilot the offering of flexible modular loads to students who need the time to build stronger foundations or pursue side interests such as entrepreneurship.

sections.label: Polytechnic and ITE internships
sections.summary: More than nine in 10 Polytechnic and ITE students today complete structured internships in the final year of their study.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: More than nine in 10 Polytechnic and ITE students today complete structured internships in the final year of their study.

sections.label: ITE enhanced curricular structure attachments
sections.summary: Under the enhanced curricular structure, ITE students will have two linked industry attachments, and ITE welcomed its first cohort of about 2,000 students.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Under the enhanced curricular structure, ITE students will be exposed to two linked industry attachments to deepen their industry exposure.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that ITE recently welcomed their first cohort of about 2,000 students under their enhanced curricular structure.

sections.label: ITE 2020 graduate employment outcomes
sections.summary: Nine in 10 ITE Class of 2020 graduates found employment within six months, with a median salary of $2,000 for full-time permanent employment, comparable to the year before.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Despite the pandemic, nine in 10 graduates from the ITE Class of 2020 found employment within six months of graduating  , with a median salary of $2,000 for those who were in full-time permanent employment, which is comparable to the year before.

sections.label: LifeSkills and graduate employment outcomes
sections.summary: Technical Diploma graduates had nine in 10 employed within six months with salaries comparable to Polytechnics, and a framework prioritising 10 LifeSkills will be strengthened through experiential opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Employment outcomes of Technical Diploma, or TD, graduates have been very promising, with nine in 10 employed within six months of graduation, and their salaries comparable to graduates from the Polytechnics.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Third, beyond the technical skills, I am pleased to inform Mr Shawn Huang and Ms Mariam Jaafar that we will strengthen our focus on softer skills and competencies, for work and life.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, this framework prioritises 10 skills, including critical thinking, collaboration, as well as mental resilience.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: These skills will prepare our students for the future workforce, where they are expected not only to excel in their domain, but also have confidence in working with their colleagues locally and globally.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: We will strengthen these skills through experiential opportunities outside the classroom, including internships, student activities and overseas exposure.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: The Polytechnics and ITE will enhance their curricula, so the incoming batch of students in AY 2022 will benefit from the enhanced baseline competencies across all 10 LifeSkills.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Building on this common framework, the Autonomous Universities will also embark on enhancements to their curricula to ensure graduates are equipped with baseline competencies in the same LifeSkills, but adapted to their student profile.

sections.label: Mother tongue language learning efforts
sections.summary: Efforts will continue to get students interested and maintain performance in mother tongue learning, with opportunities in schools and activities by the Mother Tongue Language Learning and Promotion Committees.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: At the same time, we must continue our efforts to get students interested and maintain their performance in mother tongue learning.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: We will continue to provide opportunities for our students to deepen their learning in mother tongue languages in schools, and increase their interest in mother tongue languages through activities organised by the Mother Tongue Language Learning and Promotion Committees.

sections.label: Companies send workers to training
sections.summary: Companies have sent workers to almost 245,000 places in training courses to prepare them for emerging roles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: To-date, companies have sent workers to take up almost 245,000 places in training courses, which better prepare them for emerging roles when the economy recovers.

sections.label: Singaporeans enrolled in SGUS and SGUP-CT
sections.summary: More than 22,000 Singaporeans enrolled in SGUS and SGUP-CT, and two out of three initial SGUS trainees found employment within six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: More than 22,000 Singaporeans enrolled in SGUS and SGUP-CT.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Two out of three of the initial batch of SGUS trainees found employment within six months after course completion.

sections.label: SGUS and SGUP-CT merge into SCTP
sections.summary: SGUS and SGUP-CT will merge into a new SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme from April 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: As we look towards post-pandemic recovery, we will build on our experiences with SGUS and SGUP-CT and merge these two programmes into a new SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme (SCTP) from April 2022.

sections.label: SCTP subsidies and enhanced funding
sections.summary: SCTP will be subsidised at SSG's prevailing rates, with enhanced funding of up to 90% for Singaporeans aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: SCTP will be subsidised at SSG's prevailing rates, with enhanced funding of up to 90% for Singaporeans aged 40 and above.

sections.label: Around 7,000 courses available
sections.summary: Around 7,000 courses will be available from 1 June 2022, up from around 300 today, for mid-career individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Around 7,000 courses will be available from 1 June 2022, from around 300 courses today to give mid-career individuals more options to use their credit for upskilling and reskilling.

sections.label: Companies benefit from NACE programmes
sections.summary: About 1,500 companies have benefited from the programmes offered by NACE.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: To-date, about 1,500 companies have benefited from the programmes offered by NACE.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Queen Bees companies
sections.summary: More than 930 companies, 90% of them SMEs, have participated in programmes curated by the SkillsFuture Queen Bees since its launch.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Since its launch, more than 930 companies have participated in programmes curated by the SkillsFuture Queen Bees, of which 90% are SMEs.

sections.label: SSG Skills Development Partners
sections.summary: SSG plans to partner TACs as Skills Development Partners, starting with IMDA, the Singapore Computer Society and SGTech in the ICT sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: SSG plans to partner TACs as "Skills Development Partners" to identify in-demand and emerging skills, facilitate timely dissemination of Jobs-and-Skills insights and put in place structures to accredit skills acquired at the workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: For a start, SSG will work with IMDA to partner the Singapore Computer Society and SGTech in the ICT sector.

sections.label: SkillsFuture movement goals
sections.summary: Plans were set in motion seven years ago with the SkillsFuture movement, and efforts continue towards providing opportunities for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Chairman, our plans to achieve this were set in motion seven years ago when we launched the SkillsFuture movement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We will continue to strive towards our goal of providing opportunities for all Singaporeans to develop to their fullest potential, and progress together as a society.

sections.label: TRANSIT student progress
sections.summary: About 180 students have made progress in self-management skills under TRANSIT, and every Primary school is to be supported by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Since the introduction of TRANSIT, about 180 students have made encouraging progress in developing their self-management skills.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Each can support up to 10 students in TRANSIT and we are preparing to support this number in every Primary school by 2026.

sections.label: SPED schools and SAMS
sections.summary: There are 22 SPED schools, SAMS will provide 500 Primary and 350 post-Primary places, and MOE will set up a second school in the West.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: With SAMS, there are currently 22 SPED schools distributed across Singapore to serve students with moderate-to-severe SEN.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: SAMS’ permanent site will be located next to Nan Hua High School and it will provide 500 Primary and 350 post-Primary level school places.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As part of our continued efforts to plan ahead and improve SPED school capacity, I am pleased to announce that MOE will be working with Cerebral Palsy Alliance Singapore to set up a second school in the West for students with multiple disabilities.

sections.label: COMPASS cyber kindness efforts
sections.summary: COMPASS is creating cyber kindness best practices and running capability-building sessions and "Let Us Chat!" workshops for Parent Support Group Leaders across 14 schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Recognising the impact of social media and online behaviour on our children’s mental well-being, the COMPASS team is also working to encourage a culture of cyber kindness in parents and children through creating a set of cyber kindness best practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: COMPASS has also started capability-building sessions to equip Parent Support Groups (PSGs) to support their parent community to build good relationships with their children and enhance their overall mental well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This is carried out through a series of "Let Us Chat!" training workshops for PSG Leaders, which was recently completed across 14 schools.

sections.label: More PSGs coming onboard
sections.summary: Over the next two years, more PSGs will come onboard these efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Over the next two years, we will have more PSGs coming onboard these efforts.

sections.label: MOE youth mental well-being taskforce
sections.summary: MOE is part of a whole-of-Government effort supporting youth mental well-being through the Interagency Taskforce for Mental Health and Well-being, led by Dr Janil Puthucheary.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: MOE is part of a whole-of-Government effort to support youth mental well-being through the Interagency Taskforce for Mental Health and Well-being, which is being led by Senior Minister of State for Health, Dr Janil Puthucheary.

sections.label: Singapore education confidence competitiveness cohesion
sections.summary: Singapore must embrace confidence, competitiveness and cohesion, and treat education as a continuous lifelong journey, building foundations early and supporting students in schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Singapore must therefore embrace three characteristics: to have the confidence in our abilities and ourselves, so we can keep growing and maximise our full potential; to stay competitive with the world and seize opportunities wherever they may be and, as a society, to stay cohesive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We need to move beyond seeing education as just for schools, but as a continuous journey through life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will build a strong foundation for our students from an early age, by sparking an innate curiosity and desire for lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In schools, we will support our students to discover their strengths, and hone future-ready competencies, while gaining a sense of rootedness to Singapore.

sections.label: Monitoring educators and students well-being
sections.summary: MOE is closely monitoring the mental well-being of educators and students given the exceptional circumstances at this point in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, to Mr Patrick Tay's first clarification, yes, indeed, we are closely monitoring the mental well-being of our educators and students, given the exceptional circumstances that we are in at this point in time.

sections.label: Continuous assessments replace mid-year exams
sections.summary: Instead of doing away with mid-year examinations, schools increasingly use a series of continuous assessments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To Mr Patrick Tay's second question about doing away with the mid-year examinations, what we will have – and, increasingly, we are doing this in all our schools – is a series of continuous assessments.

sections.label: Continuous and synoptic assessments
sections.summary: Continuous assessment examines students' ability to apply what they have learnt from various modules, while synoptic assessment pulls together different parts of their learning for year-end exams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: A continuous assessment examines our students' ability to apply what they have learnt based on various modules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: When it comes to the year-end exam, we have this term called the "synoptic assessment", which is that they are able to pull together different parts of what they have learnt to answer different questions.

sections.label: Purpose of testing students
sections.summary: MOE wants assessments to give feedback on how each child is doing compared with his or her previous self, not other students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If we truly, truly want our exams to be less stressful, we need to re-orientate our perspective on why we test.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And from MOE's perspective, we want all our assessments to be a feedback to our students and our parents on how their child is doing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It is how the individual child is doing vis-à-vis his previous self or her previous self, and not how he or she is doing vis-à-vis other students.

sections.label: Tests and rote memory
sections.summary: Going forward, tests will be less and less based on rote memory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Going forward, tests will be less and less based on rote memory.

sections.label: One point and continuous meritocracy
sections.summary: One point will not define a person's future forever, and continuous assessment, not a single assessment, determines achievement in life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But the assurance that we want to give to everyone is this: that one point does not and will not define a person's future forever.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We have a process of what Senior Minister Tharman called "continuous meritocracy", where it is about continuous assessment, performance that determines one's achievement in life and not just on a single point and a single assessment – that should not be our attitude, otherwise, we instil fear in our students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If our attitude and answer to the first question of why we test is – this is a self-assessment to find out the strengths and weaknesses of our students so that we can best apply the resources to help them fulfil their potential; then what we do with the test results, the definition of success for that, is that we apply the correct resources, provide the correct pathways to the students that require the necessary help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If we take that attitude of what we do with the test results and that is about providing the correct pathways to give our children the best opportunity possible, then I think exams will be less stressful.

sections.label: Stretching students appropriately
sections.summary: The aim is to make sure students are stretched appropriately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Our aim is to make sure that we stretch our students appropriately.

sections.label: Spending per child and CET
sections.summary: About a quarter of a million is spent per child in formative school years, and CET is estimated at less than 10% of MOE's budget this financial year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: The first question: Minister shared that we spend about quarter of a million per child in the formative school years and affirm that more will be invested in CET.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: And I spoke about CET currently, in this financial year, it is estimated to be less than 10% of MOE's budget.

sections.label: CET spending and SCTP
sections.summary: CET spending has increased steadily, and this year's budget will substantially strengthen CET funding through the SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Our spending on CET has increased steadily over the years and for this year's budget, what we think we will do substantially to strengthen the CET funding, is through the SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme (SCTP) that I mentioned earlier on.

sections.label: CET investment increase
sections.summary: The investment in CET will go up substantially with this year's budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: All in all, the investment in CET will go up substantially with this year's budget.

sections.label: School socio-economic mix
sections.summary: Schools should have a good mix, and most schools have good representation from different socio-economic backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: We want to make sure that there is a good mix as students learn to grow in their adolescent period and understand the real world.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: But I want to assure Mr Leon Perera that most schools have good representation from different socio-economic backgrounds – Government and Government-aided schools are largely representative of the national average.

sections.label: Independent school public housing students
sections.summary: Close to half of Independent school students come from public housing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: For Independent schools today, roughly, we have close to half of our students coming from public housing.

sections.label: Employment figure clarification
sections.summary: Nine in 10 technical diploma students get employed within six months, not ITE students.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I just want to make one clarification to my speech earlier.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: I had said that in response to Mr Sharael Taha and Dr Shahira Abdullah nine in 10 of our ITE students are employed within the first six months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Maybe it was a mix-up, because nine in 10 of our technical diploma students get employed within six months.

sections.label: MOE school start rule
sections.summary: MOE has one rule: do not start school before 7.30 am.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Actually, MOE has just one very simple rule: Thou shalt not start school before 7.30 am.

sections.label: Question asked to teachers
sections.summary: The question Dr Wan Rizal posed was asked to teachers during weekly school visits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Mr Chair, in fact, the question that Dr Wan Rizal posed, I have asked my teachers in my weekly visits to the schools.

sections.label: Teacher workload and education workforce
sections.summary: MOE will continue to lighten teachers' workload by reviewing the curriculum and applying technologies, while a cap on teachers is unrealistic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We all want in our different ways to try to alleviate the workload for our teachers by partnering them, by not overly burdening them with unrealistic expectations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But I think it is also very unrealistic for us to put such a cap on our teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That is something that speaks to the quality of our education workforce, the kind of people that we have in the system that make our education system something that we can all be proud of, that makes our education system able to continue to function, notwithstanding COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, yes, MOE will continue to see how we can lighten the workload of our teachers by making sure that we review the curriculum, applying technologies and so forth.

sections.label: Thanks to MOE ministers and officials
sections.summary: A Member thanks Minister Chan Chun Sing, other ministers, the MOE COS team and retiring Director-General Wong Siew Hoong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Having had three children, one doing "A" levels this year, one doing Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE), another doing "O" levels next year, I thank Minister Chan Chun Sing, Minister Mohamad Maliki bin Osman and Minister of State Gan Siow Huang, Minister of State Sun Xueling and the entire MOE COS team for powering this entire Committee of Supply and bringing us fresh perspectives as well as some of the policies, announcements and programmes to make our education more caring, more inclusive and more future-ready.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: At the same time, I also put on record our thanks to Director-General Wong Siew Hoong who is retiring from service at the end of this month.

sections.label: Withdrawal of amendment
sections.summary: The Member asks leave to withdraw his amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: With that, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.

sections.label: Time allocation for cuts and responses
sections.summary: Time is allocated as 40% for cuts, 50% for Ministries' responses and 10% for clarifications.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Members are aware that all of you would submit cuts.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: And the formula as to how it works is this: 40% of the time comprises your cuts; 50% of the time would comprise the response time from the Ministries; and 10% of the time allocated for clarifications.

sections.label: Guillotine times under Standing Order 92
sections.summary: Under Standing Order 92, debate on Heads of Expenditure ends when guillotine times are reached, and the Speaker fixes those times.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Pursuant to Standing Order 92, the debate on the respective Heads of Expenditure will end once the guillotine times are reached.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: In Standing Order 92(7)(a), it states that “The Speaker shall fix the time on any allotted day at which the consideration of any head of expenditure shall, if not previously disposed of, be concluded.

sections.label: MOE guillotine time
sections.summary: For MOE, the guillotine time is 1630 hours, including 20 minutes of tea time.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: As for the debate, for example, with MOE, the guillotine time is 1630 hours, incorporating 20 minutes of tea time.
